question.problem:
Solve the linear congruence $3x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,7)$ using trial and error. Express your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $7.$

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,7)$
question.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=7$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3,4,5,6$ into the congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot 0 & ≡0≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 1 & ≡3≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 2 & ≡6≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 3 & ≡9≡7+2≡2≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 4 & ≡12≡7+5≡5≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 5 & ≡15≡2\cdot 7+1≡1≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 6 & ≡18≡2\cdot 7+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡6\,(\text{mod}\,7).$

**Note**: Any number congruent to $6$ modulo $7$ is a solution. For example, note that $13≡6,$ and this also satisfies our congruence:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & ≡3\cdot 13\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡39\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡5\cdot 7+4\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡0+4\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡4\,\,✓\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$
